header.stance: 晶片股重挫、標售需求強，短天期美債領漲

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 晶片股重挫，2年期美債領漲

科技股賣壓帶動避險需求，週二美債由短端領漲。2年期標售需求強勁，讓先前因Fed立場轉鷹而下跌的短債獲得支撐；2年期殖利率單日下降8個基點至4.16%，跌幅超過週一升幅。長債反應小得多，10年期僅下降1個基點至4.50%，2年與10年期利差因此擴大至34個基點。

油價下跌有利債市，但投資人對通膨與實質利率的看法並不一致。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.21%，實質殖利率反而再升1個基點至2.29%；交換市場仍反映Fed在2027年中以前升息約45個基點。市場開始質疑的是首次升息是否需要那麼快到來。就業轉弱支持觀望，企業活動加速與售價壓力持續，卻讓升息的可能性仍然存在。

信用市場最具體的新進展，是SpaceX完成週一開始推介的首筆債券，籌得$250億。訂單規模雖大，隨著定價收緊，最終認購金額下降，買方也較偏好最短天期。2036年到期券利差比同類BBB債約高40個基點。這筆交易取得資金的同時，也顯示債權人要求補償公司距離穩定現金流仍有相當時間的風險。

## 2年期標售吸引買盤，企業調查仍有分歧

美國財政部標售$690億2年期公債，得標殖利率4.189%，為2025年1月以來同天期標售最高，需求強勁。結果帶動短端一路領先至收盤。5年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.27%，30年期下降1個基點至4.94%；2年與10年、2年與30年期利差各擴大7個基點，至34及78個基點。不過，2年期殖利率仍比一週前高11個基點，10及30年期則分別高7及1個基點。

Kevin Warsh首次主持Fed會議後，已有投資人布局債市反彈。決策隔日SOFR相關交易量倍增，不少部位押注升息幅度小於廣泛貨幣市場所反映的程度。週一至週二另有近$3,000萬投入8月買權，若美債上漲、10年期殖利率降至4.4%附近或以下，這些部位可望受惠。現券市場調查中的中性部位比重，也升至約2個月最高。投資人對立即升息有疑問，但尚未普遍轉向預期降息。

全國採購經理人初值呈現的情況，確實容得下兩種看法。綜合PMI由51.5升至52.2，服務業為51.3，製造業為55.7，製造業產出指數達57.7。另一方面，就業連續第2個月下降，工廠裁減人力的速度更是2020年以來最快。供應商交貨延誤的普遍程度創2022年8月以來最高，售價通膨則維持5月的偏高速度。企業活動改善，並未同時帶來更多用工或更順暢的供應。

區域調查也有類似落差。費城地區非製造業企業活動指數由−3.8升至2.4，銷售指數由−7.6升至19.6；全職就業卻降至−4.8，未來6個月企業展望轉負。支付價格指數降至25.8，收取價格指數反而升至20.2。里奇蒙製造業綜合指數由13降至4，出貨、新訂單與就業轉弱，投入價格漲幅卻加快。

這些資料使市場難以只憑油價下跌，就認定通膨壓力已經解除。5及7年期實質殖利率各上升2個基點，至2.03%及2.15%；20與30年期各升1個基點。10年期通膨補償下降2個基點，抵銷了實質殖利率升幅，名目殖利率才小幅走低。當天最大的行情，仍集中在對Fed升息時點較敏感的2年期。

SpaceX完成定價，也減輕了一部分供給相關壓力。市場人士曾把週一5年與10年期殖利率上升，部分歸因於這筆大額交易的避險操作。發債完成後，相關壓力減少，但當天同時有股市下跌與強勁標售，不能把整個美債漲勢都歸於避險平倉。接下來還有5年與7年期公債需要市場承接。

短期資金市場仍能消化供給。$650億42天期國庫券標售最高得標利率為3.620%，投標倍數2.91；間接投標人取得競爭性得標額的65.67%，直接投標人2.29%，交易商32.04%，最高得標利率的分配比例為92.35%。該券6月25日交割。次級市場6週期國庫券的息票等值殖利率上升4個基點至3.69%，4週期則下降1個基點至3.62%，其他短天期漲跌互見，未出現整條國庫券曲線同步上升的情況。

## SpaceX發債$250億，債權人要求額外利差

SpaceX首筆發債由週一推介的至少$200億，擴大至完成發行$250億。2036年到期券定價為美債加140個基點，比同類BBB債的平均利差約寬40個基點。訂單高峰接近$900億，定價時降至$730億，不到發行額3倍，低於今年投資級交易約4倍的平均水準；最短、風險較低的一檔最受歡迎。

公司充裕的現金，對上的是同樣龐大的未來支出。截至6月19日，SpaceX持有逾$1,000億現金，並表示有意維持投資級評等。信評機構認為，必要時公司可以縮減投資或增發股票；S&P仍預期公司會持續消耗現金至2030年，且明年支出成長快於營收，現金消耗將大幅加速。即使衛星、AI與太空資料中心的長期報酬可觀，債券利息與本金仍須按時支付。

SpaceX股價在連跌3個交易日後反彈，但對信用投資人而言，當天更有參考價值的是債券終於完成定價。最終利差及訂單自高峰回落的幅度，反映了實際成交條件。廣泛信用ETF的變化相對溫和：LQD隨美債上漲0.12%，HYG及JNK則在股市轉弱時分別下跌0.09%及0.05%。

台灣券商則為AI股投資熱潮所帶動的融資需求籌資。股票融資餘額在12個月內增加160%，券商今年已發行近$12億債券支應營運資金；資金流向股市，甚至促成6月3日央行債務工具標售認購不足。6月股票違約交割金額倍增至逾NT$20億，但仍不到交易額的0.002%；截至5月，34家活躍券商也都未超過監理限制。在政策利率維持2%的背景下，借款快速增加，仍讓券商更容易受到股市急跌影響。

巴西Raizen重整案則出現更具體的收購資金承諾。IG4 Capital表示，有足夠資本全數以現金買入債權，藉重整取得控制權。初步方案擬將約R$650億、約合$128億債務中的45%轉為約80%股權，IG4目標持股為50.1%。債權人可選擇現金、基金單位，或與日後出售連動的衍生性工具；IG4可在3月以前累積債權。現金能力讓收購構想更具可行性，但方案仍屬初步階段，各業務間如何分配價值尚未確定。

## 歐洲價格壓力稍緩，日本標售需求偏弱

歐元區綜合PMI初值由48.5回升至49.5，仍連續第3個月低於50。服務業升至48.9，製造業降至51.3，就業小幅下滑。投入成本漲幅為2月以來最低，售價通膨也降至3個月低點。價格變化稍令人安心，活動水準卻尚未顯示經濟已恢復持續成長。

ECB副總裁Boris Vujcic為6月升息1碼辯護，指出整體與核心通膨預計至2027年仍高於目標；目前整體通膨為3.2%。Philip Lane也提醒，即使中東外交取得進展，物價漲幅仍可能在一段時間內超過2%。不過，Vujcic尚未看到廣泛的工資連鎖反應，每名員工薪酬增幅放緩，中長期通膨預期也維持穩定。這使ECB必須在成本壓力減輕與通膨仍然偏高之間取捨，延續總裁拉加德認為目前不必採取更強烈行動的判斷。

日本5年期公債標售的需求則不理想。投標倍數由3.22降至3.11，低於12個月平均3.47；尾差由0.04擴大至0.06，日債期貨在結果公布後收斂漲幅。日圓貶破160兌$1，使輸入性通膨與日本央行加快升息的可能性仍受關注，儘管交換市場對年底前再升息的定價不到25個基點。油價下跌減輕一項壓力，這次需求偏弱的結果，則讓市場更關注6月25日長債續發。

歐洲另有兩項較長期的制度議題。基爾研究所估計，假設歐洲銀行與保險公司持有的美國政府債務適用20%監理風險權數，可能使區內美債需求在10年間減少約$2,000億，並使美國每年財政成本最多增加$420億。這是研究情境，尚非已實施的政策，也不能視為週二價格變化的既定原因。

歐洲議會經濟委員會則就數位歐元通過談判立場，在保障現金法償地位的同時，推進12個月的零售試驗，以及批發型央行數位貨幣的相關工作。方案未訂發行日期或持有上限。支付計畫向前推進了一步，但對銀行存款、交割資金與以美元為主的穩定幣競爭，實際影響仍待後續安排確立。

## 土耳其吸引利差交易，各國降息空間不同

美元走強之際，土耳其仍吸引外資重返。外匯利差交易部位回升至約$300億，外資持有本幣債約$150億；最近一週至少有$60億利差交易資金流入。1及3個月期里拉隱含殖利率降至32%及35%，央行提供銀行資金的利率則為40%，估計並買入約$90億外匯。資金流入有助補充外匯存底，但高本地利率與可控的地緣風險，仍是這類交易的重要條件。

匈牙利因先前福林升值改善通膨展望，反而有空間降息。央行調降25個基點至6%，將全年平均通膨預測由3月的3.8%下修至1.8%。投資人進一步反映後續降息，福林兌歐元一度下跌1.3%。摩洛哥則在食品帶動5月通膨降至1.2%後，維持利率2.25%；農業與基礎建設支出支持2021年以來最快成長，但經常帳赤字預測也擴大至2026年GDP的4%、2027年的3.8%。

巴西6月會議紀錄較為審慎。央行第3度降息25個基點、將利率降至14.25%後，整體與基礎通膨卻離3%目標愈來愈遠，官員表示可能調整降息步調。這份紀錄補充了週一債匯市場承壓的政策背景，並非再次宣布降息。

美伊談判可能帶來一筆外部資金，但使用範圍仍有限。伊朗官員表示，$120億凍結資產可望分兩筆等額釋出，美方尚未確認金額。川普則表示，任何釋出款項都只能用於向美國購買食品與醫療用品。伊朗與阿曼也表示，將研擬荷莫茲海峽協議，維持水道安全與開放；通行費用仍待協商，包括是否可能收取過路費。資金的合法用途與船舶通行成本，都還是協議經濟條件的一部分。

各國情況差異很大，廣泛新興市場債券的單日變化難以盡數反映。EMB下跌0.15%，同日美元指數上升0.39%。

## 晶片股跌勢推升美元，原油與黃金續跌

費城半導體指數重挫7.87%，Nasdaq 100下跌3.29%，S&P 500下跌1.44%。這次回檔發生在強勁漲勢之後，半導體指數一個月以來仍上漲10.49%。VIX上升12.79%至19.49，SpaceX股價則在晶片股下跌時反彈。損失雖大，主要集中在科技股；因此，企業活動調查轉強與美債避險買盤同時出現，並不矛盾。

WTI下跌2.15%至$73.21，布蘭特下跌1.05%至$77.08，兩者一個月跌幅均超過24%。能源對通膨的壓力持續減輕，但荷莫茲海峽的管理條件仍在協商，長期供給恢復的安排尚未確定。

美元指數上升0.39%至101.41，一週漲幅達1.88%。黃金下跌1.24%至$4,129.90，一週與一個月跌幅擴大至4.64%及8.65%。即使股市下跌，美元與實質殖利率上升仍對黃金不利。週二避險資金較明顯流向短天期美債與美元。

## 接下來看5年期標售，再看PCE通膨

6月24日美東時間13:00，財政部將標售$700億5年期公債；當日11:30先進行$280億2年期浮動利率券續發及119天期國庫券標售。25日13:00接續標售$440億7年期公債，11:30另有4及8週期國庫券。附息券均於6月30日交割。投標參與及交易商承接比例，將顯示2年期的強勁需求，能否延伸至週二漲幅較小的中天期。

6月25日美東時間8:30，美國同時公布5月個人所得與支出、初領失業救濟金、耐久財訂單及第1季GDP第3次估計。4月核心PCE月增0.2%、整體PCE增0.4%、支出增0.5%，所得持平。新資料將讓投資人把實際消費與通膨，對照PMI所呈現的活動加速、就業轉弱及價格壓力持續。

澳洲5月CPI在6月24日雪梨時間11:30公布，前期月增0.4%、年增4.2%。日本在25日東京時間約12:35續發約¥7,000億20年期公債，接在需求偏弱的5年期標售之後。墨西哥央行同日美東時間15:00公布決策，目前政策利率6.50%。各國物價漲勢、長債需求與披索反應，將分別呈現美國以外市場從油價下跌獲得多少緩解。

overall_summary.headline: 2年期美債領漲，SpaceX完成$250億首筆發債
overall_summary.session_narrative:
半導體股重挫7.87%，$690億2年期美債標售在4.189%吸引強勁需求，短債因而領漲。2年期收盤殖利率下降8個基點至4.16%，10年期僅下降1個基點至4.50%。油價走低，使10年期損益兩平通膨率降至2.21%，實質殖利率卻升至2.29%。市場質疑升息是否需要那麼快到來，但仍反映Fed在2027年中以前升息約45個基點。

企業調查未提供單一答案：美國綜合PMI升至52.2，就業卻再次下降，交貨延誤與售價壓力仍在。SpaceX完成$250億首筆發債，2036年到期券定價為美債加140個基點，比同類BBB債約寬40個基點。訂單由接近$900億降至定價時的$730億，最短天期最受歡迎。

日本5年期標售需求偏弱；歐元區成本漲幅減慢，ECB仍保持審慎。土耳其吸引利差交易資金，匈牙利則因先前匯率走強而有空間降息。接下來的5及7年期美債標售與6月25日PCE，將把實際需求、物價及支出，放到目前分歧的企業調查旁一起檢視。
overall_summary.summary: 半導體股下跌與強勁標售需求，帶動2年期美債殖利率下降8個基點至4.16%。10年期受實質殖利率上升牽制，變化不大；SpaceX則以較高利差完成首筆發債。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Two-Year Treasuries Rally as Chip Shares Tumble

Short-dated Treasuries rallied Tuesday as a sharp semiconductor selloff drew buyers toward safety and a strong two-year auction rewarded investors after the Federal Reserve's hawkish turn. The two-year yield fell 8 basis points to 4.16%, more than reversing Monday's increase. Longer maturities barely moved: the 10-year slipped 1 basis point to 4.50%, widening the 2s10s spread to 34 basis points.

Cheaper oil helped, but the rally exposed a divide within the bond market. Ten-year inflation compensation fell 2 basis points to 2.21%, while the real yield rose another basis point to 2.29%. Swaps still priced about 45 basis points of Fed increases by mid-2027. Traders were questioning how soon the first increase had to come, particularly as employment weakened, without abandoning the prospect of higher rates. A pickup in business activity and stubborn selling-price pressure made that distinction more than a technical one.

SpaceX meanwhile completed the financing it had begun marketing Monday, raising $25 billion in its first bond sale. The deal drew a large book, but demand shrank as pricing tightened and buyers favored the shortest tranche. Its 2036 bonds paid a spread roughly 40 basis points above comparable BBB debt. The financing was available; investors insisted on compensation for the long wait for cash generation.

## Auction Buyers Return While Business Surveys Send Mixed Signals

Treasury's $69 billion two-year auction stopped at 4.189%, the highest yield for an offering of that maturity since January 2025, and drew strong demand. The result helped the front end extend its lead into the close. Five-year yields fell 2 basis points to 4.27%, while the 30-year edged down 1 to 4.94%. Both the 2s10s and 2s30s slopes steepened 7 basis points, to 34 and 78 respectively. The two-year still yielded 11 basis points more than a week earlier, compared with increases of 7 at 10 years and just 1 at 30 years.

Investors had been positioning for some relief after Kevin Warsh's first Fed meeting. SOFR-linked volume doubled the day after the decision, with many trades favoring fewer increases than the broader money market implied. Nearly $30 million was spent Monday and Tuesday on August calls that would benefit from a Treasury rally taking the 10-year yield toward 4.4% or below. Cash-market surveys put neutral positions at their highest in about two months. These were signs of doubt about an immediate increase, rather than a consensus that the Fed would ease.

The national flash PMI gave both sides of that debate something to use. The composite rose to 52.2 from 51.5, with services at 51.3 and manufacturing at 55.7; factory output reached 57.7. Yet employment fell for a second month, and manufacturers cut headcount at the fastest pace since 2020. Supplier delays were the most widespread since August 2022, while output-price inflation held at May's elevated pace. Activity was improving even as firms reduced labor and struggled with delivery times and costs.

Regional surveys showed similar strains. Philadelphia-area nonmanufacturing firms reported an activity index of 2.4, up from -3.8, and sales of 19.6, up from -7.6. Full-time employment fell to -4.8 and the six-month firm outlook turned negative. Prices paid eased to 25.8, but prices received rose to 20.2. Richmond's manufacturing composite dropped to 4 from 13 as shipments, orders and employment weakened, even while input-price growth accelerated.

Those reports left little basis for treating lower oil as an all-clear on inflation. Five- and seven-year real yields each rose 2 basis points, to 2.03% and 2.15%; 20- and 30-year real yields added 1. At 10 years, the 2-basis-point decline in breakevens more than offset the real-yield increase and produced the small nominal gain. The large move remained concentrated in the two-year sector, where the timing of Fed action carries greater weight.

The financing calendar also became a little less crowded once SpaceX priced. Market participants had linked part of Monday's rise in five- and 10-year yields to hedging for the jumbo sale. Completion removed a source of that pressure, though it cannot account for the full Treasury rally alongside the equity selloff and auction demand. The five- and seven-year government sales still lie ahead.

Short cash markets continued to clear. A $65 billion 42-day bill auction stopped at a 3.620% high rate with 2.91 bid-to-cover. Indirect bidders received 65.67% of competitive awards, direct bidders 2.29% and dealers 32.04%; 92.35% was allotted at the high rate. The issue settles June 25. In secondary trading, the six-week coupon-equivalent yield rose 4 basis points to 3.69%, while the four-week eased 1 to 3.62% and other short maturities were mixed. The isolated increase did not spread across the bill curve.

## SpaceX Raises $25 Billion, With a Premium for Bondholders

SpaceX's debut grew from the minimum $20 billion discussed Monday to a completed $25 billion sale. Its 2036 bonds priced 140 basis points over Treasuries, about 40 basis points wider than the average for similarly rated BBB debt. Demand approached $90 billion at its peak and finished at $73 billion, less than three times the amount sold against an average near four times for high-grade deals this year. The shortest, least risky tranche attracted the strongest interest.

The premium reflects a business with substantial liquidity and equally substantial future spending. SpaceX held more than $100 billion of cash as of June 19 and has said it intends to retain investment-grade ratings. Rating firms pointed to its ability to reduce investment or raise equity if needed. S&P nevertheless expected cash burn through 2030, accelerating sharply next year as spending outpaces revenue. Bondholders must be paid along the way, even if the eventual returns from satellites, AI and space-based data centers are large.

Its shares recovered after a three-session selloff, but the bond pricing supplied the more useful new measure for credit investors. The final spread and fall from peak orders showed the terms at which the transaction actually cleared. Broad credit funds were quieter: LQD gained 0.12% with Treasuries, while HYG fell 0.09% and JNK 0.05% as equities weakened.

Taiwan's brokers were borrowing to fund a different part of the AI investment boom. Equity margin loans had risen 160% over 12 months, and brokerages issued nearly $1.2 billion of bonds during the year for working capital. Demand for equity financing had even contributed to an undersubscribed central-bank debt auction on June 3. Stock-trade defaults more than doubled in June to over NT$2 billion. They were still less than 0.002% of transactions, and none of the 34 active brokerages had breached regulatory limits as of May, but the growth in borrowing increased their exposure to a sharp market reversal. Taiwan's policy rate remained 2%.

In Brazil, IG4 Capital said it had enough capital to buy Raizen debt entirely in cash as it pursued control through the company's restructuring. The proposal would convert 45% of roughly 65 billion reais, or $12.8 billion, of debt into about 80% of the equity; IG4 was seeking a 50.1% stake. Creditors could take cash, fund units or derivatives tied to a later sale, and IG4 had until March to accumulate claims. The cash commitment made the control bid more concrete, although the proposal remained preliminary and the value split between businesses was unresolved.

## European Inflation Slows at the Margin; Japan's Auction Disappoints

The euro area's flash composite PMI improved to 49.5 from 48.5 but stayed below 50 for a third month. Services rose to 48.9, manufacturing eased to 51.3 and employment declined slightly. Input-cost inflation was the slowest since February, while selling-price inflation eased to a three-month low. The surveys offered some reassurance on the direction of prices without showing a return to sustained growth.

ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic defended June's quarter-point increase, saying headline and core inflation were expected to remain above target into 2027. Current headline inflation was 3.2%. Philip Lane also warned that price growth could exceed the 2% goal for some time despite progress in Middle East diplomacy. Vujcic saw no broad wage ripple, however: compensation per employee was slowing and medium- to long-term inflation expectations remained anchored. That left the ECB weighing softer cost pressure against inflation that was still too high, following Christine Lagarde's assessment that a more forceful response was not yet necessary.

Japan's five-year auction gave investors less reassurance about demand. Bid-to-cover fell to 3.11 from 3.22, below the 12-month average of 3.47, and the tail widened to 0.06 from 0.04. JGB futures pared gains after the result. The yen's move beyond 160 per dollar kept imported inflation and the risk of faster BOJ tightening in view, though swaps priced less than one additional 25-basis-point increase for the rest of the year. Lower oil eased one concern; the weak auction left the June 25 long-bond reopening facing closer scrutiny.

European policy work also raised longer-term questions for banks and sovereign debt. A Kiel Institute study estimated that a hypothetical 20% regulatory risk weight on US government debt held by European banks and insurers could reduce their Treasury demand by about $200 billion over a decade and add as much as $42 billion a year to US fiscal costs. The risk weight was a modeled scenario, not an enacted change or an established cause of Tuesday's trading.

Separately, the European Parliament's economic committee agreed on its negotiating position for a digital euro. The plan protected cash as legal tender while advancing a 12-month retail pilot and parallel work on wholesale central-bank digital money. It set no issuance date or holding limit. The committee vote moved the payments project forward; its eventual effect on bank deposits, settlement liquidity and competition with predominantly dollar-based stablecoins remains to be determined.

## Turkey Draws Carry Buyers as Central Banks Take Different Paths

Turkey attracted renewed foreign demand even as the dollar strengthened. FX carry positions rebuilt to about $30 billion and foreign holdings of local-currency bonds to roughly $15 billion, with at least $6 billion of carry inflows in the latest week. One- and three-month implied lira yields fell to 32% and 35%, while the central bank funded banks at 40% and was estimated to have bought about $9 billion of foreign exchange. The inflows helped replenish reserves, but their appeal depended on high local funding rates and a manageable geopolitical backdrop.

Hungary was able to move in the opposite direction after the forint's earlier appreciation improved the inflation outlook. The central bank cut 25 basis points to 6% and forecast average annual inflation of 1.8%, down from 3.8% in March. The forint fell as much as 1.3% against the euro as investors anticipated further easing. Morocco held at 2.25% after May inflation slowed to 1.2%, helped by food prices. Agriculture and infrastructure spending supported its fastest growth since 2021, although the forecast current-account deficit widened to 4% of GDP for 2026 and 3.8% for 2027.

Brazil's June minutes struck a more cautious note after its third quarter-point cut, to 14.25%. Headline and underlying inflation were moving farther above the 3% target, and policymakers said the pace of easing could change. That added a policy explanation to the bond and currency pressure reported Monday, rather than announcing another rate decision.

The US-Iran negotiations brought a possible source of external liquidity, with important limits. An Iranian official said $12 billion of frozen funds was poised for release in two equal tranches; the US had not confirmed the amount. President Donald Trump said any money released could be spent only on food and medical purchases from the US. Iran and Oman also said they would work on an agreement for the Strait of Hormuz and keep the waterway secure and open. Transit charges remained unresolved, including the possibility of a toll. Both the legal use of the funds and the cost of passage still mattered to the economic terms of a settlement.

Broad EM bond returns did not capture those differences: EMB slipped 0.15% while the dollar index rose 0.39%.

## The Chip Selloff Lifts the Dollar as Oil and Gold Fall

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 7.87%, taking the Nasdaq 100 down 3.29% and the S&P 500 down 1.44%. The selloff followed a powerful rally: semiconductors were still 10.49% higher over a month. VIX rose 12.79% to 19.49, and SpaceX shares recovered even as chipmakers fell. The losses were large, but their concentration in technology helps explain why stronger business surveys and demand for Treasuries could coexist.

WTI fell 2.15% to $73.21 and Brent lost 1.05% to $77.08, leaving both more than 24% lower over a month. The decline continued to reduce the energy pressure on inflation while negotiations over Hormuz left the terms of longer-lasting relief unsettled.

The dollar index rose 0.39% to 101.41, up 1.88% over a week. Gold fell 1.24% to $4,129.90, extending weekly and monthly losses to 4.64% and 8.65%. A stronger dollar and higher real yields worked against bullion despite the equity selloff. Tuesday's demand for safety was most visible in short Treasuries and the dollar.

## Five-Year Supply Comes Next, Then PCE Inflation

Treasury sells $70 billion of five-year notes at 13:00 ET on June 24, after a $28 billion two-year floating-rate reopening and a 119-day bill auction at 11:30. The next day brings $44 billion of seven-year notes at 13:00 and four- and eight-week bills at 11:30. The coupon securities settle June 30. Bidder participation and dealer awards will show whether the strong two-year demand extends into maturities that rallied much less Tuesday.

The June 25 US releases arrive together at 8:30 ET: May personal income and outlays, initial claims, durable-goods orders and the third estimate of first-quarter GDP. April core PCE rose 0.2%, headline PCE 0.4% and spending 0.5%, while income was unchanged. The new figures will put household demand and measured inflation beside the PMI's combination of faster activity, weaker employment and persistent price pressure.

Australia's May CPI is due June 24 at 11:30 Sydney time, following monthly and annual readings of 0.4% and 4.2%. Japan reopens roughly ¥700 billion of 20-year JGBs around 12:35 Tokyo time on June 25, following the disappointing five-year auction. Banco de Mexico announces its decision at 15:00 ET that day, with its policy rate at 6.50%. Inflation breadth, long-bond demand and the peso's response will provide separate readings on how much relief cheaper oil is bringing outside the US.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Short Treasuries drew buyers as semiconductors fell 7.87% and the $69 billion two-year auction attracted strong demand at 4.189%. The two-year closed 8 basis points lower at 4.16%, while the 10-year slipped only 1 to 4.50%. Cheaper oil lowered 10-year breakeven inflation to 2.21%, but the real yield rose to 2.29%. Markets questioned the urgency of a Fed increase while still pricing about 45 basis points of tightening by mid-2027.

Business surveys offered no simple answer: the US composite PMI improved to 52.2, yet employment fell again and supply delays and selling-price pressure persisted. SpaceX completed a $25 billion debut, with the 2036 bonds paying 140 basis points over Treasuries, about 40 above comparable BBB debt. Orders fell from nearly $90 billion to $73 billion by pricing, and buyers favored the shortest tranche.

Japan's five-year auction disappointed, while euro-area cost inflation eased alongside continued ECB caution. Turkey drew carry inflows and Hungary cut rates after earlier currency strength. The next tests are the five- and seven-year Treasury auctions and June 25 PCE data, which will put actual prices and spending beside the uneven business surveys.
